$comment: Shared CSS Module scoped-class-name conformance table.
One rule, two implementations that cannot share code, and a project is
compiled by both of them in the same build:
- crates/ruvyxa_bundler/src/style_module.rs   (emits the stylesheet)
- packages/ruvyxa/runtime/compiler.mjs        (emits the class map the
server renderer imports)
The stylesheet comes from one and the class attribute in the rendered HTML
comes from the other, so a name they disagree on is not a mismatch anybody
sees as an error: the page renders with a class no rule matches and the
styles are simply absent. Nothing fails a build and nothing appears in a log.
They had disagreed. Both fold the project-relative path before hashing it —
`reject_case_colliding_css_modules` in crates/ruvyxa_bundler/src/compiler.rs
states why: the same file must hash identically across case-insensitive
filesystems. JavaScript folded with `String.prototype.toLowerCase`, which is
the whole Unicode default case conversion; Rust folded with
`str::to_ascii_lowercase`, which leaves every non-ASCII letter alone. On a
case-insensitive filesystem `Ü/card.module.css` and `ü/card.module.css` are
one file, and Rust hashed them as two — so a project with any non-ASCII
uppercase letter in the path to a `.module.css` file rendered unstyled, and
the collision guard that exists to catch exactly this under-reported as well.
Full Unicode folding is the shared behavior, because it is the one the guard
already claims and the one a case-insensitive filesystem actually performs.
`relativePath` is the path from the project root, and the hash input is
`{folded relative path}:{local}` — so a case can be replayed against any
root, which is what lets the Rust test use a synthetic one and the
JavaScript test a real temporary directory.
Every implementation replays this file:
- crates/ruvyxa_bundler/src/style_module.rs        (Rust test)
- tests/packages/ruvyxa/compiler.test.mjs          (JavaScript test)
Add a case here first when changing how a scoped class name is minted; a
port that drifts then fails in the language that drifted rather than in a
browser looking at an unstyled page.
$formatNote: A scoped name is `{stem}_{local}__{digest}`. The stem is the file name with
its extension and a trailing `.module` removed and every character that is
not ASCII alphanumeric replaced by `_` — it is a readability affordance and
is deliberately *not* case-folded, so it can differ from the folded path the
digest is taken over. The digest is FNV-1a/64 over the UTF-8 bytes of
`{folded relative path}:{local}`, lowercase hex, padded to 16 characters.

cases.$why: The plain case, and the golden the Rust side already carried alone.
ASCII case is folded for the digest and kept for the stem, so this shares a digest with the case above and not a name.
A non-ASCII uppercase letter in a directory. This is the case the two implementations disagreed on.
The same letter in the file name, which also pins that the stem replaces it rather than folding it.
